observation_summary: The FastDateFormat 'z' pattern (timezone name) always prints the system default timezone instead of the timezone associated with the Calendar instance passed to the format() method.
reasoning_summary: The bug was caused by the TimeZoneNameRule class using a cached TimeZone instance (the one associated with the FastDateFormat object) instead of dynamically retrieving the TimeZone from the Calendar object provided at runtime. The fix involved removing the cached field and modifying the appendTo() method to extract the TimeZone from the calendar instance, which is a correction of the procedural logic used to determine the timezone display name.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'TimeZoneNameRule class stopped respecting the Calendar instance's timezone, and instead now always uses the mTimeZone of the FastDateFormat instance itself'
The fix diff shows the removal of the 'zone' field from TimeZoneNameRule and the addition of 'TimeZone zone = calendar.getTimeZone();' inside the appendTo() method.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves changing how the rule interacts with the Calendar object, the root cause is the internal logic of the rule (the algorithm) that determines which timezone to display, rather than a mismatch in the interface contract itself.
